speaker: village
text: Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a013
text: Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 1).

speaker: a014
text: Zinn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a015
text: Fina gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Nessa, the pile's gone and I didn't get a piece of it — I came to you first before I figure out what that means. You took three, which is right, and Bram took three, which surprises me a little — tell me what you know about his morning before we decide anything.

speaker: a013
text: Bram took three because he came in at one food and couldn't afford to look weak going into a year with Mako sitting on two — I think he moved fast while the pile was still fat and didn't ask anyone's permission, which is either him finally trusting his own judgment or him deciding he doesn't owe us the conversation first. What worries me more is you walking in empty-handed: you're the heaviest person in this village even without the pile, but a year is long and Mako knows how to count. Come find me after dark and I'll give you one from what I'm holding — quietly, not where anyone can watch the direction of it.

speaker: a015
text: After dark is good — I'll find you. But Nessa, I've got twenty food already and I'm the target you're naming, so before we move anything around, I want to know whether Mako's spoken to you this morning or whether his two from the pile is the only move he's made so far.

speaker: a013
text: Mako hasn't come to me this morning — his two from the pile and his silence since is the whole of what I've seen from him, and that stillness is the part I don't trust. A man who took three last year and pulled back to two this year is either being careful about how he looks, or he's already decided the pile isn't where the food he wants is coming from.

speaker: a015
text: That last part is what I keep coming back to — a man with his strength who pulls back from the pile isn't going hungry, he's going quiet, and quiet Mako is the version I've been afraid of since Roan died. I want to talk to Zinn before dark, before you give me that food, because if she knows anything about what her father's thinking she'll tell it to me before she tells it to anyone else.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn will tell you what she knows, but she'll tell it sideways — she never names her father flat out, she circles it and lets you read between. Go to her, but go easy and give her something first, a word or a food, because Zinn talks more when she doesn't feel like she's being asked to choose.

speaker: a015
text: A word it is, then — I'll find something kind to say about Sela and let that open the door, because Zinn's soft on her sister and that's the easiest way in. Nessa, if she tells me anything that changes what I think about tonight, I'll come to you before I act on it, not after.

speaker: a013
text: Good — come to me first, always, before you act on anything Zinn says about him, because she loves him and she loves us both and that means she'll soften whatever she tells you without meaning to. The thing I want you to hold going into that conversation is this: Mako gave Zinn food twice last year, and a man doesn't feed his daughter out of sentiment alone when he's sitting light on food — he's buying something, and I want to know what it is before you're alone with her and she hands you a half-truth dressed up as a warning.

speaker: a015
text: I'll carry that with me — Mako feeding Zinn when he was sitting light isn't kindness, it's a ledger, and I want to know what he thinks she owes him before she's standing between us and him without knowing it. Go careful today, Nessa, and don't let Bram see how much you're watching his food — a man who just took three is counting who noticed.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, before you go to Zinn — one thing I want said between us that I haven't said to anyone else: if Mako makes a move this year, not a raid but a conversation, the kind where he comes to you alone and makes it sound like sense, don't answer him on the spot, not even no. Bring it to me first, because the answer that sounds right in the moment he's standing in front of you is the one he's already planned for.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Bram, Nessa, Fina to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, you took three from the pile and I took none — I'm sitting at zero food and one satiation, and if I don't eat before the year turns I don't wake up. I'm asking plainly: can this circle spare one food for the woman who's been feeding it?

speaker: a013
text: Esa, you've fed Bram through three lean years and you're not dying on my watch — take one from me right now, no question.

speaker: a003
text: Nessa, I'm taking it and I won't forget this — that's two debts I carry to this household now, and I intend to repay both. Bram, I need to hear from you too, not because I doubt Nessa, but because a circle that only speaks through its youngest voice isn't standing the way I thought we were.

speaker: a015
text: Esa, Nessa's already put food in your hand and that's settled — but I want to add something to what you said to Bram, because you're right that a circle that doesn't speak isn't standing: Bram took three this morning without a word to any of us first, and I'm not counting that against him, but I want it named in this room so we all know it happened. What I'm watching now is whether Mako saw how fast Bram moved and what he's decided that means.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, Fina's right that it needs naming, and I'll say what Fina didn't: you moved before any of us spoke and took what a man your strength could take, and I'm not ungrateful for what this household has given me today, but I need to know whether this circle shares a thought before it shares a pile, or whether I'm buying protection from people who've already made their own count. Say something.

speaker: a001
text: I moved fast because the pile was going and one satiation means I don't make it to next year half-fed — that's not a count against this circle, that's a man keeping himself standing so he can be worth something when Mako moves. Three is what I need to eat and hold through a long year, not what I took to hoard. Esa, you've got food in your hand now and I'll match Nessa's word: if you're short before the year turns, you come to me before you go hungry.

speaker: a003
text: Bram, I hear you, and I'll take your word at the same value I've been giving it — which is the only currency this circle actually runs on. But I'll name the thing you didn't name: if Mako took two and you took three and Nessa took three, that's more than half the pile in three hands before the rest of us blinked, and I'm not saying your reasons were wrong, I'm saying we need to agree before next year opens that we move with a thought between us, not just fast. That's the circle I'm paying into, not the other kind.

speaker: a001
text: Esa, you're right, and I'll hold to it — next year the pile opens with a word between us before anyone moves. But right now I want to know whether Mako said anything to either of you this morning, because a man who took two and kept his mouth shut while the rest of us talked is either patient or he's already decided something.

speaker: a003
text: Mako said nothing to me — not a word, not a look — and that's the answer I trust least, because silence on a man with two bloodlines and three food in hand means he's already past the talking stage. What I want from this room before it closes is a simple thing: if Mako comes to any one of us alone, we don't answer alone. We find each other first.

speaker: a001
text: Esa's rule is the right one and I'll hold to it — Mako comes to any one of us, we stall him and find the others before a word goes back. Fina, you're the one he'll approach first if he moves, so I want you to know the stall before you need it: tell him you'll think on it, tell him your stomach's unsettled, tell him anything, but don't answer alone. Nessa, you're closer to her door than I am — stay that way.

speaker: a003
text: Fina, I hear Bram's instruction and I'll give you mine on top of it: if Mako comes to you before you can find us, look at what he's offering and count it twice, because a man who spent three years silent and fat doesn't open his mouth unless the number already works for him. That number is the thing we need before we can answer it. Don't give him a yes or a no — give him a question back, any question, and buy us the hour we need to think together.

speaker: a001
text: Fina, one more thing while the four of us are still the only ears in the room — you gave food to Mako last year, and I need to know whether that was your choice or his ask, because those are two different things and I'd rather hear the honest answer from you now than find out the shape of it when he comes to your door.

speaker: a015
text: Fina gives 1 food to Esa.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 2 food to Zinn.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gathers Dell to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Dell, pile's empty again and I've got twelve food — better than I expected, and I want you to have some of it before the day gets complicated. Tell me what you know about Fina and Bram this year, because she was feeding him twice over by the end of last year and a woman who does that either decided he's her wall or she's been told a story that made it feel like one.

speaker: a011
text: Twelve from you and zero from me — tell me your number first so I know what you can spare, because I walked away from the pile empty and I'm sitting at satiation two and that's the thing I fix before I say another word about Fina or Bram. After that: Fina fed Bram four times last year that I counted, and not one of those times did she ask him for anything back, which means she's not trading with him, she's tithing, and a woman who tithes to a man like Bram has already decided he's the one who decides whether she's safe.

speaker: a009
text: Take two now, Dell — I've got twelve and you're at satiation two, which means you eat first and we talk after. On Fina: tithing to Bram without asking anything back is the part that worries me most, because a woman who doesn't ask for the return hasn't decided he's her wall yet, she's still deciding, and that means we're not too late — but we won't be early much longer.

speaker: a011
text: I'll take the two and eat one now so you can watch me stop worrying about my own number and start worrying about hers. Fina came into this year with nineteen food and no father and she's already feeding Bram and Esa both — she's buying a crowd, not a wall, and a woman building a crowd out of grief hasn't chosen a side yet, she's chosen to not be alone. That's the door I want to walk through today, and I want to bring something when I knock — not food, not words about Bram, just my time, because the one thing nobody in this village has given her since Roan went is someone who sat down and had no reason to.

speaker: a009
text: Then go to her today, before Bram's had time to count what she gave him last year and show up looking like he remembers. I'll stay visible so you're not walking in as the only name watching her — and if she asks about me, tell her I knew her father and meant it when I said he stood when it counted.

speaker: a011
text: I'm going now — and Ryn, if she feeds me while I'm sitting with her, I'll know she's been practicing that gesture so long it's become reflex, and reflex is what you break before it becomes loyalty.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Fina to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Fina, I sat with your father once in a lean year when nobody else would and he talked about you the whole time — not your food count, not your strength, just you, and I've been meaning to find you since he went but I kept letting other things push in front of it, and I'm sorry for that.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile's gone again and Mako walked away with two before the dust settled — same as last year, same man, same calculation. I need to know what you two are holding and whether either of you is thinking about what happens when he decides sitting quiet isn't enough anymore.

speaker: a002
text: I'm holding eight, Kael, and I've been thinking about nothing else since the pile went empty — Mako took two this year but Nessa took three and Bram took three, and that's the household that worries me now as much as Mako does. What I want to know is whether you've spoken to Bram since last year, because the word he gave in our rooms hasn't been tested and a man with six food and fifty-eight strength who's been fed by Nessa and Esa both is running his own arithmetic whether he says so or not.

speaker: a004
text: Bram I haven't spoken to since that year he said he was looking for a door — and I believed him then, but a man who walks away from two fights doesn't stay patient forever, especially when Nessa's been feeding him hand to mouth like she's keeping him for something. What worries me isn't Bram alone — it's Bram and Nessa and Fina moving as one, which is three bodies and food enough to sit comfortable while the rest of us scrape. Esa, you've been quiet and you've been feeding him — I need to know if that's because you think he's yours or because you owe him something I don't know about.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I'll let you answer Kael's question, but while you're thinking I'll say what I'm sitting with: Bram and Nessa and Fina as one household is nineteen food and a hundred and sixty-two strength, and that's not a wall I can stand against if they decide I'm on the wrong side of it — which means everything I've spent keeping Bram friendly either pays off in the next bad year or it was the longest losing trade of my life. Kael, the thing I need from you before this room closes is whether you're willing to stand somewhere Mako and Bram can both see you standing, because a man with fifty-four strength and no food debt to either of them is rarer than either of those two know.

speaker: a004
text: I'll stand where they can see me — that's not the question. The question is whether standing means anything without Esa in it, because two people visible is a warning, but one man alone is just a target they've already counted. Esa, I'm asking you plain: are you in this room or are you in Bram's?

speaker: a002
text: Esa's been quiet long enough that I'm starting to read the silence myself — and what I'm reading is a woman who's given too much to Bram to walk away clean, which means she's not choosing between this room and his, she's waiting to see which one costs her less. Esa, I'm not asking you to abandon a trade you've already made, I'm asking you to stand visible with Kael and me before Mako runs the numbers and decides that Bram's household is the only wall worth standing near. That's a different ask, and it costs you nothing you haven't already paid.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I've watched you feed Bram six times this year and say nothing in return for any of it, and I've stayed patient — but Vela just handed you the easiest ask anyone's made of you in thirteen years, and if you can't meet it, I need to know that now so I stop counting you as weight I can lean on. Standing visible costs you one conversation and nothing else. Tell me you're in it.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I've been watching you for thirteen years and I know the difference between a woman thinking and a woman who's already decided — so I'll make this simple: if you're in this room, say it now and I'll split my eight food three ways before dark to prove this circle means something, but if you're waiting to see which side lands softer, then say that too, because I'd rather know and plan around it than carry a weight that isn't there.

speaker: a004
text: Vela's offer is the realest thing said in this village in years — eight food split three ways is a cost she doesn't have to pay, and she's paying it — so Esa, I'll match it with the only thing I have, which is my name and my body standing next to yours when the counting starts, and that's worth more than food when Mako or Bram starts looking for who's alone.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I've said everything I have to say and I'm not adding another layer — the offer's on the table and it doesn't get better than this, so the next voice in this room should be yours.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, I've lived fifty-seven years and I've learned to read a room that's gone quiet, and this one has — so I'll say it one last time and not again: you're holding one food and no allies, and a woman alone with one food in year fourteen doesn't see year fifteen.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I'm closing this room in one breath: take the food, stand with us, and the three of us walk into year fourteen together — or stay quiet, and I'll know you've made your choice without saying it, and I'll plan around a circle of two.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Nessa, Zinn to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, I gave you two before I called this meeting, so your number's not the one I'm sitting with — Nessa, you took three from the pile this morning and Bram took three and I watched you feed each other all last year, and I need you to say out loud, right now, whether Bram knows what you're holding and whether that's why he took three. I'm not your enemy and I'm not Bram's enemy, but I cannot protect this family from a deal I don't know the terms of.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, Sela's asking the right question and so am I — you and Bram moved food back and forth all year like a settled pair, and if there's a deal there, I'd rather know it from you than watch it play out in front of us. I'm not going to push you the way I used to, but I need to know if Bram's counting your food as partly his, because if he is, that changes what we can do with it.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, you've gone quiet on us in this room more times than I can count and I have kept choosing to believe it's caution and not distance — but I'm forty-five next year, your sister is twenty-eight, and if Bram has a claim on your food or your loyalty that runs deeper than this family does, I need to know it now while I can still do something about it.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I've watched you give to Bram more times than I can count and watched him give back, and I don't think that's nothing — but I also don't think it makes him yours or you his, and the thing Sela and I need to hear isn't whether you love him, it's whether he's got a hand on your counting. Say it plain: does Bram know your number before you move it, or does he just know your face?

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, I've been forty-four years old since this morning and I'll be forty-five when the next pile comes, and what that means is that this is the last year I can give you a sibling — so I need you to understand that when I ask you what Bram knows about your counting, I'm not asking because I want to take something from you, I'm asking because if he's in your ear when you decide how to move your food, that matters to me more this year than it has ever mattered before.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I've said my piece twice already and I meant it both times — so I'm going to stop talking and let Sela's last words sit, because she just told you something she can't unsay and it deserves more than my voice on top of it.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, I've run out of patient words and I've run out of clever ones — so here's what's left: you are my daughter, Bram is your father's rival and a man who has tried to raid this family twice, and if this is the year I can still make a child, I need to know whether the blood I'm building toward has a clean path or one that runs through him first.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I meant what I said about stopping — but Sela just named the thing I didn't have words for, and I can't stay quiet on top of it. If Bram's your father and your partner both, that's a knot I don't know how to stand inside of, and I need you to help me understand it before this year moves any further.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, stop — "your father and your partner both" isn't a knot, it's a mistake, and I won't let that word sit in this room unchallenged. Nessa's father is Bram, yes, but Fina's father is Roan, and what I've watched this year isn't a daughter sleeping with her father — it's a daughter who made a deal she won't name. Nessa, I'm not accusing you of anything worse than silence, but I need the silence to end right now, because the shape of what Zinn just said is going to spread past this room if you don't give me something true to replace it.

speaker: a014
text: Sela's right and I was wrong to say it that way — I'm sorry, Nessa, that came out crooked and I didn't mean it. What I meant, and what I still mean, is that Bram is your father's blood-rival and a man who moved to raid us twice, and if you've made a deal with him, I need to understand the shape of it — not because I'm judging you, but because Sela's running out of years and I need to know whether the circle I'm standing in has a hole in it.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, Zinn apologized and I forgive her the same breath I'm asking you to forgive me for letting this room get loud — but the question underneath all of it is still standing, and it's a simple one: does Bram know your number, yes or no.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I've apologized once and I won't do it twice — but the question Sela just stripped bare is the one I've needed answered since last year, and I'm asking you to honor it: does Bram know your number, yes or no, because everything this family does next hangs on that single word.

speaker: a015
text: Fina gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a003
text: Esa gives 1 food to Bram.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn, the pile ran dry before half the village got there and you're sitting on four — that's too thin going into a long year, and I'm giving you one of mine before anyone starts watching who has what. I want to know what happened with Fina; she's got eighteen still and she gave food to Bram twice last year, which means she's building something with him, and I need to know if that door is already closed before I stop thinking about it.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Fina.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Fina.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Fina gave two to Bram last year and one to Esa, which isn't nothing, but she also gave me one and she's still feeding Nessa — that's not a woman who's closed a door, that's a woman spreading weight while she decides. I'll go to her through Nessa this year, and I mean it this time, not just a plan we keep naming.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 2 food to Dell.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gathers Dell to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Go, Dell — and don't come back and tell me what she said, come back and tell me how she looked when she said it, because Fina's a woman who's been watching this village count her food since before her father's body was cold and she's learned to say the right thing to whoever's sitting across from her.

speaker: a011
text: I hear you — and I'll bring you back her face, not her words, because you've taught me that's where the truth lives. One more thing before I go: you're at twelve and I'm at two, and I want you to eat before you give anything else away today, even to me, because the day's long and I need you standing when I come back with what I find.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Mako.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Fina.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Sela just put one in my hand and Zinn's sitting steadier now — that's good, but I want Zinn to hear me say this flat: go to Nessa today, not tomorrow, because Bram's got three food and he's been feeding Nessa all year and a man with something to offer doesn't wait while another man builds the path. If Fina's still open, she won't stay that way much longer.

speaker: a007
text: Sela gives 1 food to Nessa.

speaker: a015
text: Fina gives 1 food to Bram.
